sections.h2: Closing costs a Michigan seller pays by law
sections.html:
Three charges are fixed by statute: two deed taxes and a recording fee. State deed tax runs $3.75 for every $500 of value, with a leftover partial block billed as a whole one. County deed tax is 55 cents per block. The exception is the largest county class, where commissioners may set a rate as high as 75 cents.

Agent commissions, title insurance, attorney charges and utility proration are negotiated in your listing agreement and purchase contract, so they change from one sale to the next. The three statutory charges stay put.

sections.h2: How the deed tax is figured
sections.html:
Count how many $500 units the deed price holds, rounding a partial unit up. Multiply that count by $3.75 for the state tax, then by 55 cents for the county tax in a typical county. Your total is the two added together.

The deed must show the full value of the real property, or an affidavit attached to it must. If land and movable items like equipment sell together, only the land is taxed provided the two values are listed separately. Treasury prepares the affidavit form for the state tax. The State Tax Commission prepares the county one.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed tax and when
sections.html:
MCL 207.523 makes the grantor liable. Send the payment to your parcel's county treasurer within 15 days of handing over the deed. In most closings the attorney or escrow officer subtracts it from your proceeds and remits it.

Your purchase contract can push this cost to the other side, which is why every line of the settlement statement deserves a read before closing day. A buyer who covers the tax instead of the seller may file the refund request later.

sections.h2: Deeds exempt from the state tax
sections.html:
MCL 207.526 lists many exempt instruments. These are the ones that come up most for people selling a home:

  • Any deed where the price paid is under $100.
  • A parent deeding to a son, daughter, stepchild or adopted child, or deeding to a grandchild in one of those groups.
  • A transfer between spouses that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties.
  • A court judgment or order that directs a transfer without setting a dollar price.
  • A deed that comes out of a mortgage foreclosure or stands in for one. When the foreclosing party resells, that sale is taxed.
  • A corrective quitclaim that repairs a defect in title the grantee already holds.
  • A land contract under which the vendor holds legal title until the final payment.

The county act, MCL 207.505, runs a parallel list that leaves out the child and grandchild exemptions, so have your closing agent check the deed against both.

Sometimes. If you or the buyer paid and the deed met an exemption on the day it was signed, you can apply to Treasury for the money back. The refund right reaches back to transfers made in the four years before the amendment that created it.

One refund route is aimed at homeowners. Paragraph (u) of MCL 207.526 applies when the seller had claimed the principal residence exemption, the parcel's state equalized value had not risen above its value on the first tax day after occupancy or purchase (whichever came later), and the price was set by arm's length negotiation. Before you sign the deed, have your closing agent test your sale against that rule.

Recording a single document costs $30 flat, however many pages it runs (MCL 600.2567). The same section also prices these add-ons: $1 a page for copies, $5 to certify a recorded document, and records searches at 50 cents per year searched with a $5 minimum.

Charter counties can set their own schedule by ordinance or resolution, though never above their cost of providing the service. Phone the recording office covering your parcel before mailing a deed. An electronic filing must be paid for within one business day after the office receives it.

A land contract where legal title stays with the vendor until the price is fully paid owes no deed tax (MCL 207.526(o)). Property tax is different. A land contract signed after 1994 is a change of ownership under MCL 211.27a(6)(b), and taxable value resets the following year. Recording the deed at payoff does not reset it again.

Paragraph (v) of that section exempts a foreclosure deed or deed in lieu from the state tax. The lender's own resale is not covered. Behind on your mortgage? Ask the county treasurer how the deed you are weighing would be taxed before you sign.

sections.h2: Property taxes after the house sells
sections.html:
After closing, the buyer gets 45 days to send the local assessor a transfer notice, on a State Tax Commission form that lists the parties, date, actual price and parcel number. Each month at minimum, the recording office sends the assessor a list of recorded transfers.

MCL 211.27a says a change of ownership raises taxable value to full state equalized value starting the next January. Giving the house to a spouse skips the reset. Since 2014 so does a residential transfer to a parent, child, sibling or grandchild who keeps the use non-commercial. How this year's bill is divided is a contract matter, shown as the proration line on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What to bring and what happens at closing
sections.html:
Ask the closing agent for a draft settlement statement early. Match the three statutory lines against the table above. Then review the lines your contracts drive: commission, title work and how the property tax bill is split.

  • Bring a payoff letter from your lender if a mortgage is still open.
  • Have documents ready for any exemption you plan to use, such as proof of the family tie on a deed to a child.
  • Check the purchase agreement to see which side pays the deed tax.
  • Confirm the county treasurer gets paid inside the 15-day window after delivery.

A cash sale has no buyer's lender, so no lender-ordered items need settling. Deed taxes and the recording fee are still owed, paid from your proceeds.

faqs.q: How are deed taxes figured on a Michigan sale?
faqs.a: Count the $500 units in the sale price, rounding a partial unit up. Each unit carries $3.75 of state tax plus 55 cents of county tax, as long as the county has fewer than 2,000,000 residents.

faqs.q: Is the buyer or the seller responsible for the deed tax?
faqs.a: Seller, by default. The statute puts it on the grantor, and it usually comes out of the seller's proceeds. Your purchase agreement can assign it differently.

faqs.q: How much does Michigan charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars per document is the statutory base, and certifying a copy costs extra. A charter county may post its own schedule.

faqs.q: Does gifting the house to my daughter or son create deed tax?
faqs.a: The state side is exempt: paragraph (j) of MCL 207.526 covers a son, daughter, stepchild or adopted child, and paragraph (k) covers grandchildren. MCL 207.505 for the county tax has no matching paragraph, so ask the treasurer about that half.

faqs.q: What is the payment deadline for the tax?
faqs.a: Within fifteen days after the deed is delivered. The money usually comes out of closing funds.
